fullPassage:
You are the narrator of your own life. The tone and perspective with which you describe each experience generates feelings associated with that narration. For example, if you find yourself constantly assuming, “This is hard,” “I wonder whether I’m going to survive,” or “It looks like this is going to turn out badly,” you’ll generate (a) anxious feelings. It’s time to restructure the way you think. Underlying this narration are the beliefs that (b) frame your experience and give it meaning. Think of your beliefs as having many layers.
On the surface are your automatic thoughts. These are like short tapes that momentarily flash through your mind. Call these automatic thoughts a form of “self-talk” that you use as you navigate through the day. You (c) produce a wide variety of these automatic thoughts, some consciously and some unconsciously. For example, automatic thoughts that (d) relieve anxiety go something like this: You walk into a room, see a few new people, and say to yourself, “Oh, no, I don’t like this. This is not good.” Or, “These people will soon find out that I am full of anxiety and will reject me.” Automatic thoughts are bad habits that (e) cloud fresh and positive experiences. They can turn a potentially good experience into one fraught with anxiety. If you tell yourself that you are always stressed or full of anxiety before doing something new, that new experience will be tainted by that anxiety.

For example, if you find yourself constantly assuming, “This is hard,” “I wonder whether I’m going to survive,” or “It looks like this is going to turn out badly,” you’ll generate (a) anxious feelings. It’s time to restructure the way you think. Underlying this narration are the beliefs that (b) frame your experience and give it meaning. Think of your beliefs as having many layers.
On the surface are your automatic thoughts. These are like short tapes that momentarily flash through your mind. Call these automatic thoughts a form of “self-talk” that you use as you navigate through the day. You (c) produce a wide variety of these automatic thoughts, some consciously and some unconsciously. For example, automatic thoughts that (d) relieve anxiety go something like this: You walk into a room, see a few new people, and say to yourself, “Oh, no, I don’t like this. This is not good.” Or, “These people will soon find out that I am full of anxiety and will reject me.” Automatic thoughts are bad habits that (e) cloud fresh and positive experiences. They can turn a potentially good experience into one fraught with anxiety. If you tell yourself that you are always stressed or full of anxiety before doing something new, that new experience will be tainted by that anxiety.
questions.stem: 이 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 주제: 자동적 사고(부정적 자기 대화)가 긍정적 경험을 불안으로 오염시키는 과정
det.analysis:
✅ ④ 자동적 사고가 새로운 경험을 불안으로 오염시키는 메커니즘: 글 전체의 핵심
❌ ① 자동적 사고의 종류와 분류 방법: 분류가 아닌 영향을 설명
❌ ② 불안 장애의 진단 기준: 의학적 내용 아님
❌ ③ 스트레스 해소를 위한 구체적 방법: 구체적 방법은 제시하지 않음
det.tip: 주제: automatic thoughts(자동적 사고) + cloud/taint + anxiety

ch: 자동적 사고가 새로운 경험을 불안으로 오염시키는 메커니즘

questions.stem: 밑줄 친 부분이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 밑줄 친 ‘짧은 테이프처럼 순간적으로 마음을 스쳐 지나간다’의 함축: 자동적 사고는 깊이 생각하지 않고 빠르게 지나가는 반사적 반응

❌ ② 자동적 사고는 오래 지속되는 깊은 성찰이다: short + momentarily와 반대
❌ ③ 자동적 사고는 음악처럼 즐거운 경험이다: 부정적 맥락
❌ ④ 자동적 사고는 논리적으로 계획된 사고이다: automatic(자동적)과 모순
det.tip: 비유 해석: short tapes(짧은 테이프) = 반복적이고 자동적인 것, momentarily flash = 순간적

ch: 자동적 사고는 짧고 빠르게 지나가는 반사적 반응이다.
